note: Per-cloud cut-outs of the G-Tomo A_RVS cube (Lallement et al. 2022 dust map, RVS band, A_rvs = 0.5385 A_0; file Arvs_gtomo_shaped.npy, 161 x 161 x 17 at 50 pc, x = 4122..12122 pc Galactocentric, y = -4000..4000 pc, z = -379.2..420.8 pc) at its full 50 pc resolution: cumulative extinction from the Sun to each voxel, stored as one byte per voxel, A_rvs = byte x 0.02 mag (the cube peaks at 4.60 mag, so nothing saturates). Axes are Sun-centred kpc: u = x - 8.122 (away from the Galactic centre), v = y, w = z - 0.0208; voxel (i, j, k) sits at (u0 + 0.05 i, v0 + 0.05 j, w0 + 0.05 k), flat index i*ny*nz + j*nz + k. Each box covers the zoomed field (2 x hw_deg of arc wide, +-0.75 hw_deg in latitude) out to three times the cloud distance (at most 2.4 kpc) inside the dust slab. Cloud positions: SIMBAD (l, b) from the paper list; d_kpc as stated in d_src; map_peak_kpc is where A rises fastest along the cloud sightline in this cube. The shipped 50 pc midplane map in dust_l22.json is this cube's z = 20.8 pc slice.
